text:
mike.h: Starting RFC follow-up thread on kernel autotune heuristics. TL;DR: want a conservative default that adapts to heavy tail seq-lens, but avoids spiky warmup overheads. Open Qs: bucket granularity, prefill vs on-request warmup, cache invalidation strategy. thoughts?

anya: +1 on conservative default. We saw regressions when buckets are too fine-grained; kernel churn hurts latency p99.

sam: Can we sketch concrete numbers? e.g., buckets = [16,32,64,128,256] vs exponential? Prefill budget = 4k tokens?

devon: From perf tests: fine-grained buckets help throughput but increased OS kernel launches + memory churn. exponential buckets (powers of two) hit a sweet spot.

mike.h: Proposal sketch:
```yaml
bucket_strategy: exponential
buckets: [8,16,32,64,128,256]
warmup_mode: staged_prefill
warmup_tokens_per_bucket: 4096
prefill_parallelism: 2
cache_policy: prefix_kv_lru
```
Staged prefill = prefill small buckets eagerly, larger ones on demand with async background prefill.

emily: How do we measure warmup cost? We need a single metric: warmup_tokens_consumed_per_request and warmup_time_ms. Also specify a hard cap so we don't exceed GPU memory.

sam: Also need fallback when prefill fails (OOM or timeout). Fallback to smaller-quantized kernel or cold-path with low concurrency and a "grace" delay to avoid thundering herd.

devon: Agree. Also suggest opportunistic reuse: if a preceding request already warmed a compatible kv cache (prefix match >= 50%), treat as warmed.

mike.h: On caching: two knobs: prefix-KV caching (shared across requests) and transient per-batch caching. For multi-tenant dedicated customers, default to per-tenant isolated cache, but allow cross-tenant read-only dedupe for identical prompts?

anya: Policy complexity is high. Maybe start with three simple policies: disabled, per-tenant, global-readonly. Default = per-tenant. Revisit if customers ask.

infra-bot: CI perf tests scheduled: kernel-autotune-warmup-v2 on queue. Results ETA 2026-04-02.

emily: One more: telemetry. We need sampling to avoid heavy metrics. Log warmup events with reason tags (prefill, on-demand, reuse, fallback). That will help tune.

mike.h: Action items:
- devon: run power-of-two vs linear buckets perf suite and share numbers (due Fri)
- sam: draft fallback policy and OOM handling (PR)
- emily: instrument warmup metrics + cap enforcement
- anya: update RFC note with simple defaults

mike.h: Anything else? :thinking_face:

anya: Add a small note about model variants: fallback to a quantized kernel should preserve logits ordering; need regression tests.

sam: +1. I'll add tests for numerical deltas <= 1e-3.

mike.h: Great. If no objections I'll fold this into the RFC and propose default config.

emily: :thumbsup:

devon: :rocket:
